papers.title: Topology of Reasoning: Understanding Large Reasoning Models through Reasoning Graph Properties
papers.review_note: Uses hidden-state reasoning graphs to study cyclicity, diameter and small-world structure. Evidence about graph properties does not establish that matching four surface-language labels teaches human reasoning.
papers.review_scope: Focused reading of full-text methods, experiment setup, evaluation and relevant appendix passages; not a proof-by-proof reproduction or a claim of cover-to-cover reading.

papers.title: S-GRPO: Early Exit via Reinforcement Learning in Reasoning Models
papers.review_note: Early-exit reward design controls redundant reasoning; on-policy batches contain 128 prompts times eight responses. Report both correctness and generation length.
papers.review_scope: Focused reading of full-text methods, experiment setup, evaluation and relevant appendix passages; not a proof-by-proof reproduction or a claim of cover-to-cover reading.

papers.title: Consistent Paths Lead to Truth: Self-Rewarding Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
papers.review_note: Uses consistency and volatility of intermediate-state representations as intrinsic rewards. Compare structural signals against representation-based, label-free alternatives.
papers.review_scope: Focused reading of full-text methods, experiment setup, evaluation and relevant appendix passages; not a proof-by-proof reproduction or a claim of cover-to-cover reading.

papers.title: Prismatic Synthesis: Gradient-based Data Diversification Boosts Generalization in LLM Reasoning
papers.review_note: Gradient-space data diversity is studied across hundreds of runs. Dataset diversity and generalization need their own evidence beyond prompt count.

papers.title: Incentivizing Dual Process Thinking for Efficient Large Language Model Reasoning
papers.review_note: Adaptive fast/slow reasoning uses explicit tags, a cold-start stage and RL. Isolate explicit process supervision from the effect of subsequent RL.
papers.review_scope: Focused reading of full-text methods, experiment setup, evaluation and relevant appendix passages; not a proof-by-proof reproduction or a claim of cover-to-cover reading.

papers.title: ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in Large Language Models
papers.review_note: Prolonged RL uses 136K examples and more than 2,000 training steps, with training-stability interventions. This is one recipe, not a universal required update count.
papers.review_scope: Focused reading of full-text methods, experiment setup, evaluation and relevant appendix passages; not a proof-by-proof reproduction or a claim of cover-to-cover reading.

papers.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
papers.review_note: Uses broad pass@k evaluations to distinguish probability concentration from capability expansion. Include base-model sampling baselines before claiming new reasoning capacity.
papers.review_scope: Focused reading of full-text methods, experiment setup, evaluation and relevant appendix passages; not a proof-by-proof reproduction or a claim of cover-to-cover reading.

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: Dissecting Mathematical Reasoning for LLMs Under Reinforcement Learning
papers.review_note: SPARKLE separates plan following, subproblem solving and other reasoning components. Final-answer accuracy alone does not establish a change in reasoning process.
papers.review_scope: Focused reading of full-text methods, experiment setup, evaluation and relevant appendix passages; not a proof-by-proof reproduction or a claim of cover-to-cover reading.

papers.title: Beyond Verifiable Rewards: Scaling Reinforcement Learning in Language Models to Unverifiable Data
papers.review_note: JEPO addresses unverifiable, long-form targets; uses 64 prompts and four generations per update. Difficulty of verification does not imply keywords are an adequate quality reward.
papers.review_scope: Focused reading of full-text methods, experiment setup, evaluation and relevant appendix passages; not a proof-by-proof reproduction or a claim of cover-to-cover reading.

papers.title: SWE-RL: Advancing LLM Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning on Open Software Evolution
papers.review_note: SWE-RL trains 1,600 steps with 32 problems and 16 rollouts per batch. Real software engineering requires execution-based, external evaluation even when training rewards are cheaper.
papers.review_scope: Focused reading of full-text methods, experiment setup, evaluation and relevant appendix passages; not a proof-by-proof reproduction or a claim of cover-to-cover reading.

papers.title: Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models

papers.title: Beyond the 80/20 Rule: High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
papers.review_note: Studies high-entropy tokens and token-selective policy gradients, including substantial within-batch optimization. State the unit of every reported training step.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning in Large Language Models with One Training Example
papers.review_note: One-example RLVR can still involve approximately 1,400 or more training steps. Few unique training questions do not imply few generated responses or little optimization.

papers.title: Act Only When It Pays: Efficient Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning via Selective Rollouts
papers.review_note: Selective rollout sampling addresses uninformative zero-variance groups. Track rejected samples and rollout cost; select checkpoints using a separate validation split.

papers.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Negative Reinforcement in LLM Reasoning

papers.title: Revisiting Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning from A Cross-Domain Perspective

papers.title: GVPO: Group Variance Policy Optimization for Large Language Model Post-Training
